§1
Warm-Up · Module Quick-Fire
One question per session · Activate the whole module · Badge 🔥
8 min

S1A → S4A — One question each. No notes.

FROM S1A — Reception & Arrival
You arrive at Vertex Logistics for a meeting. The receptionist asks "Good morning — how can I help you?" Say your full arrival introduction in 3 sentences. Use to be + possessives + there is.
FROM S2A — Routines & Small Talk
Your US colleague asks: "What does your typical Monday look like?" Answer in 3 sentences using always, usually, never — and correct adverb position.
FROM S3A — People & Descriptions
Introduce one real colleague — their job, personality (2 adjectives), appearance (has), and what they're really good at. Include a possessive 's sentence.
FROM S4A — Directions & Tour
Give 4-step directions from your company entrance to your desk. Use imperatives + past/through/opposite/on the left. No hesitation.
Teacher Note
Run this as a rapid-fire round — 45 seconds per question, no preparation. Students speak immediately. Write errors on board (don't correct yet). After all 4: "Which session was hardest to remember?" Use their answers to decide which grammar section in §5 needs most attention today.
8 min · 4 questions · 2 min each · Badge 🔥 when done
§2
Speaking · The Full Vertex Scenario
3 integrated rounds · All sessions · All structures · One building
10 min
T–S · Role-play
You are Ana García, Week 4 at Vertex. A Chicago executive visits today. You greet them at reception, introduce yourself and your manager Carmen, give 3 steps to the meeting room, and mention one problem (the printer is broken). Use structures from ALL 4 sessions.

"Good morning! I'm Ana García — I'm the project coordinator. I'm here to see you — welcome to Vertex! This is Carmen López, my manager. She's very organized and really good at logistics. The meeting room is on the third floor — follow me, this way please. Oh — there's a small problem: the printer isn't working today. I'm sorry — we can't print the agenda."

S1A+S2A+S3A+S4A in one 6-sentence sequence

S–S · Elevator scene
Partner A: you're Ana in the elevator with the Chicago executive. Make 90 seconds of natural small talk — your routine, the team, the building. Use adverbs of frequency + descriptions + 2 colloquial phrases. Partner B: respond naturally as the executive.

"How was your flight? I usually arrive at 8:45 but today I'm always early when we have visitors! Our team is really great — David's always very creative, and Marcos is never late. Let me check my schedule — I think we have coffee before the meeting."

all 4 sessions integrated naturally in small talk

Class · Integration race
Each student: in 60 seconds, use structures from ALL 4 sessions in one connected story about their real company. Teacher counts: 1 point per correct structure used. Highest score wins. Target: 8+ structures. Go around the room.

Target structures (8 points): to be + job · always/usually/never · adjective before noun · has + appearance · possessive 's · there is/are + preposition · can/can't · direction imperative
Each structure = 1 point. 8+ = full integration achieved. Certificate unlocked.

Teacher Note — Integration Round
After Round 3: tally scores on the board. Ask the student with the highest score to repeat their story. The class identifies each structure as they hear it. This is the most powerful moment of the entire module — students hear a peer doing it right, in their own words, at their own level.

§5
Grammar Review · Error Correction + Drag to Order
Top errors from S1A–S4A · Find the mistake · Fix it · Integration check
12 min
SessionStructureTop ErrorCorrect Form
S1A to be + a/an + job "I am coordinator." ✗ I am a coordinator. ✅Always a/an before singular job title
S2A adverb of frequency "I check always my emails." ✗ I always check my emails. ✅Adverb before main verb
S3A has + appearance "She is short hair." ✗ She has short hair. ✅HAS for physical features, not IS
S4A preposition of direction "It's in the left." ✗ It's on the left. ✅Always ON the left/right — never IN
✏️ Activity A — Spot & Fix the Error
1. "Good morning — I am engineer at Vertex. I have meeting with Mr. Torres."
2. "She is usually busy, and she is always check her emails first."
3. "Marcos is very reliable and he is short dark hair."
4. "Go straight, turn right at the corner — it's in the left, at the end."
✏️ Activity B — True or False? Integration Check
"She's a very organized coordinator" — adjective order is correct.
"I never am late" — correct position of NEVER with to be.
"The room is in front of the elevator" — correct use of "in front of."
"Go to straight and past the printer" — correct direction instructions.
§6
Listening · Ana's Month at Vertex — Full Integration
~190 words · All 4 sessions · All structures · Pre-listening map task · Badge 🎧
10 min
Ana's Month at Vertex — Full Integration
A1.1 · M6 · S5 · Voice: ElevenLabs · Speed: 0.78
0:00 0:00

Hi! I'm Ana García, and today is the end of my first month at Vertex Logistics here in Celaya. I want to tell you about my experience.

When I arrived on my first day, I went straight to reception. There was a problem with my badge — it didn't work on the fourth floor. David Torres, the operations manager, helped me. He's very friendly and always very busy. His desk is always full of papers, but he's never late. David's office is opposite the break room, at the end of the corridor.

My manager is Carmen López. She's a very organized and quite strict coordinator — but fair. She has long black hair and she's always very professional. Carmen's meetings are always on Mondays. I usually attend and I always take notes. I sometimes work overtime on Tuesdays, but I never miss a deadline.

Last week, I gave my first tour to a supplier from Chicago. I was nervous! "This way, please — follow me," I said. "The cafeteria is just around the corner — you can't miss it." It went really well. The supplier said my English was very good. Actually — that made me very happy!

I can speak English at work now. I can give directions, introduce my team, and describe our building. I can't do everything yet — but I can do a lot. And I'm not done learning.

📎 ElevenLabs: Voice — Ana (American English) · Speed 0.78 · A1.1 M6 S5 · ~190 words · All M6 session structures integrated

Teacher Note — Pre-listening Integration Task
Before playing: "I'm going to play Ana's story. Your job is to count: How many structures from S1A do you hear? S2A? S3A? S4A?" Listen twice. After: tally on board. The script is designed to contain at least 3 clear examples of each session's grammar. Students who find all 12+ structures earn a bonus point toward the Exit Task rubric.
1. What problem did Ana have on her first day?
2. How does Ana describe Carmen López?
3. True or False: Ana sometimes works overtime on Tuesdays.
4. True or False: Ana says she can do everything in English now.

Exit Task · The Vertex Integration Challenge
Performance task · 4 min · Rubric · Badge 🎓
20 min
🎓 Exit Task — A1.1 Module 6
You Are Ana García — Month 2 Begins
A new intern from the US arrives at Vertex Logistics today. You are the host. In 4 minutes, you must:

1. Welcome them at reception (arrival + introduction)
2. Introduce yourself and describe a colleague (descriptions + possessive 's)
3. Give a quick building tour — at least 3 locations with directions
4. Mention your typical work routine using frequency adverbs
5. Handle one problem (elevator/printer/badge) using can't + need
6. Close naturally with a colloquial phrase from the module

📊 Rubric — Click Each Cell to Score

Click a cell to select the score for each criterion. 1 = needs work · 2 = developing · 3 = achieved

Criterion1 — Needs Work2 — Developing3 — Achieved
Arrival & Intro (S1A) Incomplete — missing article or to be Complete but hesitant Fluent, natural, correct article use
Routine & Frequency (S2A) Adverb position wrong or missing Correct position, limited vocab 3+ adverbs, all in correct position
Descriptions (S3A) "Is" instead of "has" for appearance Correct HAS, no possessive 's HAS + adjectives + possessive 's used
Directions (S4A) No imperatives, wrong prepositions Imperatives used, some prep errors Clear route, correct movement + place preps
Fluency & Colloquial Long pauses, no colloquial phrases 1 colloquial phrase, some flow 2+ phrases, natural flow, good pace
Teacher Note — Exit Task Debrief
After each student: share the rubric score immediately. Say: "Your strongest moment was [X]. One thing to work on: [Y]." 30-second feedback per student. Then: the whole class votes on who had the most natural small talk (not most grammar) — this separates correction from communication. The student with the most natural delivery, not fewest errors, gets the class award.
